feature: Journal startup without retaining two decoded reader states
implementation: Validate and drop each decoded slot, retain generation/slot/checksum descriptors, then reload and compare the selected slot before publication.
assertions: Only the selected slot is reloaded after inspection
Changed checksum or generation, disappearance and read failure reject opening
A newer checksummed unsupported state version falls back to the older valid slot
Saving after fallback overwrites the invalid slot and reopens successfully
Existing torn-slot, output-limit, frame-format, settings and progress-journal tests pass
commands: nix-shell --run 'cargo fmt --all && cargo test --locked -p femto-reader --lib --test journal && cargo test --locked -p femto-sync && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features desktop,femto-catalog/tailnet --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check'

firmware_manifest.installation_status: No automatic installer. Verify the actual device partition table and recovery backup before installation.

tradeoff: One additional read and JSON decode of the selected slot in exchange for avoiding simultaneous retention of both decoded states.
limitations: Memory lifetime follows the implementation; no allocator instrumentation or physical heap measurement
Reload-change tests inject slot-read results, not physical concurrent SD writes
Single-owner contract remains; no filesystem locking added
No new full workspace, native simulator, independent-peer suite or grayscale build
